newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Zim Israel Navigation chief expected to resign.
newsitem.headline: Zim Israel Navigation chief expected to resign.

text.p: The president of Zim Israel Navigation, Matty Morgenstern, is expected to hand in his resignation sometime on Wednesday, sources close to the company said.
A spokeswoman for Zim, Israel's biggest shipping company and one of the world's 10 largest, would not comment on the reports but said a statement was due later on Wednesday.

Israel Corp chairman Shoul Eisenberg controls 51 percent of Zim through Israel Corp and the rest is controlled by the government of Israel. Zim is rumoured to be one of the companies the government is considering selling this year.
News of the expected resignation emerged as Eisenberg was beginning a major reorganisation of Zim following widening losses, the sources said. Morgenstern has headed Zim for 12 years.

The sources speculated that Eisenberg and his son Erwin, who acts as chief executive officer of Israel Corp, were looking to turn Zim around after the company began making losses in the second quarter of 1996.
In the third quarter alone, Zim lost $6.3 million on revenues of $351.1 million, bringing the nine-month loss to $2.1 million.
The sources said the Eisenbergs were expected to take a more active role in managing the company.
